conclusion: Round 2 (task version 2) ran seeds 7, 19 and 31 with 10% test-label outliers of magnitude 10 and unchanged training data. Across all three seeds the linear model showed lower error than the baseline on mse, mae and median_absolute_error; the gap between linear and baseline was largest for median_absolute_error (linear ~0.21-0.28 vs baseline ~3.04-3.53) and mse (linear ~10.16-10.27 vs baseline ~19.71-23.95), while mae differences were smaller (linear ~1.25-1.28 vs baseline ~3.57-3.87). Round 1 evidence (experiment-0001, clean data, seed 7 only) is preserved and not overwritten; round 2 evidence is experiment-0002 with fresh per-seed CSVs. This synthetic exercise does not establish scientific quality.
limitations: This is a synthetic workflow test fixture, not a real human meeting decision, and it does not establish scientific quality or generalizability.
Only three seeds (7, 19, 31) were run, so variance estimates are coarse and no formal significance testing was performed.
Outliers were injected only into test labels at a single fraction (0.1) and magnitude (10); other fractions, magnitudes, and training-label contamination were not explored.
Results are reported for a single task version and model family (linear vs baseline); no hyperparameter tuning or alternative models were evaluated.
Round 1 and round 2 use different data conditions (clean vs 10% test-label outliers), so their metric values are not directly comparable.
